title.name: Stone by Stone
title.subtitle: Climb and restore the palace of Olite
menu.normal.note: Five hearts for all five climbs.
menu.duo.note: Tied with a rope: help each other up. You only get there together!
menu.solo.note: Alone: use the crates to reach the high ledges.
intro.1: Olite, 1813. The story goes that during the war against Napoleon, the palace of the kings of Navarre burned and fell into ruin.
intro.2: Many years later, two young stonemasons arrive with a rope, a mallet and plenty of spirit.
intro.3: Climb together, stone by stone: walls, gardens, galleries and towers. Gather the golden stones to restore it all!
outro.1: The banner of Navarre flies from the highest tower. The palace of Olite shines again!
outro.2: You can visit it for real today: much of it was rebuilt from 1937 on, following what was left standing.
level.walls.name: The town wall
level.walls.where: From the moat up to the wall walk
level.walls.tip: Jump up through the ledges and break rubble with your head or your mallet [B].
level.gardens.name: The hanging gardens
level.gardens.where: Orange-tree terraces high on the walls
level.gardens.tip: Old trellises give way, so keep moving! Shoo the storks with your mallet.
level.gallery.name: The King's Gallery
level.gallery.tip: Watch out for loose roof tiles! They wobble for a moment before they fall.
level.winds.name: Tower of the Four Winds
level.winds.where: A tower open to every wind
level.winds.tip: Gusts of wind push you about. Wait for them to pass before you jump.
level.crowns.name: Tower of the Three Crowns
level.crowns.where: The very top of the palace
level.crowns.tip: The last climb! Plant the banner of Navarre at the top, together.

fact.title: Did you know?
fact.charles: Charles III the Noble, king of Navarre from 1387 to 1425, enlarged the palace of Olite and made it his grand residence.
fact.gardens: The palace had hanging gardens high on its walls. It is said that orange trees grew there.
fact.gallery: The King's Gallery has Gothic arches carved into the stone like lace, open onto the gardens.
fact.winds: The Tower of the Four Winds is said to take its name from its lookout, open on all four sides.
fact.crowns: The Tower of the Three Crowns is one of the palace's tallest. Its name is thought to come from its stepped top.
fact.fire: The story goes that in 1813 the palace was burned so French troops could not use it.
fact.restore: From 1937 the palace was slowly restored. Part of what you see today was rebuilt in those years.
fact.storks: Every spring, storks nest on the towers and bell towers of southern Navarre.
fact.lions: The story goes that exotic animals, lions among them, were kept at the palace of Olite to amaze the court.
